Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:10:1.hebrew: סך מקרי דרדקי - מנין תינוקות הראויין למלמד אחד:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:10:1.english: The sum [of students] for a teacher of children - The number of children that is appropriate for one teacher.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:10:2.hebrew: ריש דוכנא - שומע עם התינוקות מפי המלמד, וחוזר ומשגירו בפי התינוקות, ואותו ריש דוכנא נוטל שכר:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:10:2.english: The head of the platform - He listens together with the children to the teacher's words, and then repeats them and drills them into the children's mouths; and this head of the platform takes payment.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:10:3.hebrew: ומסייעין ליה ממתא - לשכור לו אותו ריש דוכנא:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:10:3.english: And they assist him from the town - To hire for him that head of the platform [i.e., the assistant teacher].

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:11:1.hebrew: דילמא אתי לאיתרשולי - יתפאר בלבו שאין כמותו, ויתרשל מן התינוקות, ולא יירא שמא יסלקוהו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:11:1.english: Lest he come to become negligent - He will take pride in his heart that there is no one like him, and will become lax with the children, and will not fear that they might remove him.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:11:2.hebrew: כל שכן - כשחשבנוהו, יתן לב להיות למד יפה, שדואג מקנאת חבירו שסלקוהו מפניו, שיביישנו בבני העיר:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:11:2.english: All the more so - When we have counted him [as a teacher], he will take care to teach well, because he is concerned about the jealousy of his fellow, who was removed on his account, [and fears] that he will shame him before the townspeople.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:12:1.hebrew: דגריס ולא דייק - שלומד הרבה, ולא דייק בלימוד התינוקות שלא ישתבשו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:12:1.english: Who teaches much [lit., "grinds"] but is not precise - Who teaches a great deal, but is not careful in teaching the children, [to ensure] that they do not err.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:1:1.hebrew: סיפא אתאן לתינוקות של בית רבן - ואע"ג דקול הבא מחמת אחרים לא מצי מחויי:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:1:1.english: In the latter clause we have come to the children of the teacher's house - Even though [the neighbor] cannot object to a sound that comes by way of others [i.e., the noise of the children, which is caused by third parties rather than by the teacher himself].

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:1:2.hebrew: משום תקנת יהושע בן גמלא - אחד מן הכהנים הגדולים שעמדו בבית שני, כדאמר ביבמות (דף סא):
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:1:2.english: Because of the ordinance of Yehoshua ben Gamla - He was one of the High Priests who served in the Second Temple, as stated in Yevamot (page 61).

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:2:1.english: And you shall teach them - The father himself is commanded to teach him.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:3:1.hebrew: פלך - הרבה מדינות בפלך אחד, והוא לשון אפרכייא:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:3:1.english: District - Many provinces [are included] in one district, and it is an expression for an eparchy.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:5:1.english: Rav Shmuel bar Shilat - He was a teacher of children (above, Bava Batra 8b).

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:5:2.hebrew: ואספי ליה - האכילהו והשקהו תורה בעל כרחו, כשור שנותנין עליו עול על צוארו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:5:2.english: And stuff him - Feed him and give him Torah to drink against his will, like an ox upon whose neck a yoke is placed.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:5:3.hebrew: לא תמחייה אלא בערקתא דמסנא - ברצועות של מנעלים, כלומר מכה קלה שלא יוזק:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:5:3.english: You should strike him only with the strap of a shoe - With the straps of shoes; that is, a light blow, so that he will not be harmed.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:5:4.hebrew: ליהוי צוותא לחבריה - אינך זקוק לייסרו יותר מדאי, ולא לסלקו מלפניך, אלא ישב עם האחרים בצוותא, וסופו לתת לב:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:5:4.english: Let him be a companion to his fellow - You need not discipline him excessively, nor remove him from before you; rather, let him sit together with the others, and in the end he will take it to heart.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:6:2.english: A craftsman - One who lets blood (a bloodletter).

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:6:3.hebrew: מעכבין עליו - מפני שמרבה עליהן קול, נכנסין ויוצאין:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:6:3.english: They may prevent him - Because he increases the noise for them [with the students] coming in and going out.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:8:1.english: To a Jewish scribe - A teacher of children.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:8:2.hebrew: בסופר מתא - מלמד תינוקות העיר, ומושיב מלמדים תחתיו, והוא מורה את כולם איך יעשו, ויש שם קול גדול:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:8:2.english: With the town scribe - The teacher of the town's children, who seats [other] teachers under him, and he instructs all of them how to proceed, and there is a great noise there.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:9:1.hebrew: מתקנת יהושע בן גמלא ואילך - שישבו מלמדי תינוקות בכל עיר:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:9:1.english: From the ordinance of Yehoshua ben Gamla onward - That teachers of children were established in every city.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:9:2.hebrew: לא ממטינן ינוקא ממתא למתא - ללמוד מיום ליום, שמא יוזק בדרכים, שהשטן מקטרג בשעת הסכנה, שנאמר "פן יקראנו אסון" (בראשית מ״ב:ד׳). אלא יוכל לכוף בני אותו מתא להושיב מלמדי תינוקות:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:9:2.english: We do not bring a child from town to town - to learn from day to day, lest he be harmed on the roads, for the Satan prosecutes at a time of danger, as it is stated: "Lest harm befall him" (Genesis 42:4). Rather, [a person] may compel the people of that town to establish teachers of children.

Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:9:3.hebrew: תיתורא - גשר רחב. וחבירו במנחות (דף לה.): תיתורא דתפילין — מקום מושבם, שדומה לגשר:
Rashi on Bava Batra 21a:9:3.english: Titora - A wide bridge. And its counterpart is in Menachot (35a): "the titora of the tefillin" — the place where they sit, which resembles a bridge.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:10:1.hebrew: סך מקרי דרדקי כ"ה ינוקי - אבל פחות מכאן, אין בני העיר יכולין לכוף זה את זה להשכיר להם מלמד:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:10:1.english: The total for a teacher of children is twenty-five children - But [with] fewer than this, the residents of the city cannot compel one another to hire a teacher for them.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:2:1.hebrew: זכור אותו האיש לטוב ויהושע בן גמלא שמו - הוא אותו האיש דאמר רב יוסף (ביבמות דף סא.): תרקבא דדינרי עיילא ליה מרתא בת בייתוס לינאי המלך עד דאוקים ליהושע בן גמלא בכהני רברבי. וצדיק גמור היה, כדאשכחן הכא. והא דקאמר התם (שם): קטיר קא חזינא הכא — לפי שהיו אחרים חשובים ממנו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:2:1.english: "That man is remembered for good, and Yehoshua ben Gamla is his name" - He is the same man about whom Rav Yosef said (in Yevamot 61a): Marta daughter of Baytus brought a *tarkava* (a measure) of dinars to King Yannai until he appointed Yehoshua ben Gamla among the high priests. And he was a completely righteous person, as we find here. And as for what is said there (ibid.), "I see a knot [of conspiracy] here" — [that is] because there were others more distinguished than he.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:2:2.english: "U'lemadtem otam" [and] "u'lemadtem atem" - Some books do not have the reading "u'lemadtem atem" ("and you shall learn, you yourselves"), and [the Gemara] derives [the teaching] from the fact that it is written "u'lemadtem" ("and you shall learn"), which implies [that you shall learn] on your own:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:3:1.hebrew: כי מציון תצא תורה - לפי שהיה רואה קדושה גדולה וכהנים עוסקים בעבודה, היה מכוון לבו יותר ליראת שמים וללמוד תורה, כדדרשי' בספרי: "למען תלמד ליראה וגו'" — גדול מעשר שני שמביא לידי תלמוד. לפי שהיה עומד בירושלים עד שיאכל מעשר שני שלו, והיה רואה שכולם עוסקים במלאכת שמים ובעבודה, היה גם הוא מכוון ליראת שמים ועוסק בתורה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:3:1.english: "For from Zion shall go forth Torah" - Because he would see great sanctity, and priests engaged in the Temple service, he would direct his heart more toward fear of Heaven and toward learning Torah, as we expound in the Sifrei: "So that you may learn to fear etc." — [this shows that] great is the second tithe, for it brings one to [Torah] study. For he would remain in Jerusalem until he had eaten his second tithe, and he would see that everyone was engaged in the work of Heaven and in the [Temple] service; so he too would direct his heart toward fear of Heaven and engage in Torah.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:4:1.hebrew: כבן שש כבן שבע - כבן שש בבריא, כבן שבע בכחוש:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:4:1.english: Like a six-year-old, like a seven-year-old - Like a six-year-old for a healthy child; like a seven-year-old for a frail one.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:5:1.hebrew: בבציר מבר שית לא תקבל - והא דתנן במסכת אבות (פ"ה מכ"א): בן חמש שנים למקרא — בבריא לגמרי, כדאמר בכתובות (דף נ. ושם): הלומד בנו פחות מבן שש, רץ אחריו ואינו מגיעו. ואיכא דאמרי: חבריו רצין אחריו ואין מגיעין אותו. ותרוייהו איתנהו — דחליש וגמיר. ואיבעית אימא: הא בכחוש והא בבריא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:5:1.english: "For [a child] younger than six, do not accept [him]" - But as for what we learned in tractate Avot (5:21): "A five-year-old [is ready] for Scripture" — [that refers] to one who is completely healthy, as it says in Ketubot (50a): One who teaches his son [Torah] before the age of six runs after him and never catches up with him. And there are those who say: his peers run after him and do not catch up with him. And both [statements] hold true — [for a child] who is weak but learns [well]. Or, if you wish, say: this one [applies] to a frail child, and that one to a healthy child:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:6:1.hebrew: אחד מבני מבוי כו' - פי' רשב"א: דלא גרס "מבוי" אלא "חצר", דאי גרס "מבוי" תיקשי לאביי דשרי בחצר אחרת. וההיא ד"עושה אדם חנות בצד חנות של חבירו" שרי לכל הפחות בחצר אחר, ורבא נמי לא פליג עליה, אלא דמוקי מתני' דשריא אף באותה חצר, והכא אסר אפילו בחצר אחרת. אלא "אחד מבני חצר" גרס:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:6:1.english: "One of the residents of an alley," etc. - Rashba explained that [the text] does not read "alley" but "courtyard," for if it read "alley," it would be difficult for Abaye, who permits [competing] in a different courtyard. And that [source] about "a person may set up a shop next to his fellow's shop" permits it at the very least in a different courtyard, and Rava too does not disagree with him; rather, he establishes the Mishnah as permitting even in the same courtyard, whereas here [the baraita] forbids even in a different courtyard. Rather, the text reads "one of the residents of a courtyard."

Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:6:2.hebrew: וגרדי - וא"ת: ומאי שנא גרדי מבעל ריחים, דתנן במתני' דאין יכול למחות בידו ולומר "איני יכול לישן מקול הריחים ומקול הפטיש"? וי"ל: דמתני' בעושה לעצמו, והכא בגרדי העושה לאחרים, דאיכא נכנסין ויוצאין. וא"ת: הא אמרי' בסמוך "האי בר מבואה דאוקי ריחייא כו'", דינא הוא דמעכב עליה משום דאמר ליה "קא פסקת לחיותי"; משמע דאי לאו משום דקא פסקת לחיותי, היה יכול להעמיד שם הריחים, אע"ג דעושה לאחרים. ולקמן נמי תניא: "עושה אדם חנות בצד חנותו של חבירו כו'", דאף על גב דאיכא נכנסין ויוצאין טובא. ודוחק לחלק דהתם כבר יש יוצאין ונכנסין לריחים הראשון או לחנות הראשון. וי"ל: דהתם בחצר אחרת שרי. א"נ מתני' נמי בעושה לאחרים, ובריחים ובקול הפטיש אין נכנסין ויוצאין כל כך, שנותנין לו פעם אחת וטוחן; אבל בגרדי יש הרבה יוצאין ונכנסין, שהרבה מביאין לו מטוה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:6:2.english: And a weaver - And if you ask: What is the difference between a weaver and a mill owner, regarding whom we learned in the Mishnah that [the neighbor] cannot protest against him and say, "I cannot sleep because of the sound of the mills and the sound of the hammer"? And one can answer: The Mishnah is speaking of one who works for himself, whereas here [it speaks of] a weaver who works for others, so that there are people entering and exiting. And if you ask: But we say shortly below, "This person of the alley who set up mills, etc.," [and] it is right that [the other] can prevent him, because he can say to him, "You are cutting off my livelihood"; this implies that were it not for the fact that "you are cutting off my livelihood," he would be permitted to set up the mills there, even though he works for others. And further on it is also taught: "A person may set up a shop next to his fellow's shop, etc.," even though there are many people entering and exiting. And it is forced to distinguish that there, there are already people entering and exiting to the first mill or the first shop. And one can answer: There, in a different courtyard, it is permitted. Alternatively, the Mishnah too speaks of one who works for others, but with a mill and the sound of the hammer there are not so many people entering and exiting, since [a customer] gives to him once and he grinds; but with a weaver there are many people entering and exiting, since many bring him spun thread.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:8:1.hebrew: ולא לסופר ארמאי - משמע דאם לא סופר הוה שרי להשכיר לארמאי. וא"ת, דאמרי' בהגוזל בתרא (ב"ק דף קיד.): האי בר ישראל דזבין ליה ארעא לעובד כוכבים אמיצרא דבר ישראל חבריה — משמתינן ליה, דא"ל: אריא ארבעת אמיצראי. ודוחק לחלק בין מכר לשכירות. ונראה לר"י, דהתם כשישראל רצה לקנות, אבל אם אין ישראל רוצה לקנות — מותר:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:8:1.english: "And not to an Aramean scribe" - This implies that if he were not a scribe, it would be permitted to rent to an Aramean. And if you ask: But we say in the last chapter of Bava Kamma, in [the chapter] Hagozel (114a): This Jew who sold land to a gentile, [land] bordering the boundary of another Jew, his fellow — we excommunicate him, for [the neighbor] can say to him: "A lion has crouched at my boundaries!" And it is forced to distinguish between selling and renting. And it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak (the Ri) that there [the case is] where a Jew wanted to buy [the land]; but if no Jew wants to buy it — it is permitted:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:8:2.hebrew: בסופר מתא - אין נראה לפרש כפ"ה דסופר מתא היינו מלמד תינוקות של כל העיר, דאיכא קול גדול. דהא לקמן אמר רבא: "מקרי דרדקי וסופר מתא כמותרין ועומדין" — כיון דאשמועינן דמקרי דרדקי הוי פסידא דלא הדר, ה"ה מלמד כל תינוקות העיר, ואמאי איצטריך תו למינקט סופר מתא? ואין לפרש נמי כפ"ה בהמקבל (ב"מ דף קט:): סופר מתא מספר אנשי העיר, דהא קרי הכא בברייתא "סופר". אלא נראה כמו שפי' ר"ח: סופר מתא — כותב שטרות העיר, ולהכי חשיב ליה לקמן פסידא דלא הדר, אם נכתב השטר שלא כדין:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:8:2.english: "A scribe of the town" - It does not seem correct to explain, like the Rashi commentary [lit. Perush HaKuntres], that "scribe of the town" means a teacher of all the children of the town, because there is a great noise [that he causes]. For below Rava says: "A teacher of children and a scribe of the town are considered as [already] permitted and standing [i.e., they may be freely established]" — since [the Gemara] teaches us that with a teacher of children there is a loss that cannot be recovered, the same would apply to a teacher of all the children of the town, so why would it need to mention "scribe of the town" in addition? Nor can one explain, like Rashi, as in the chapter HaMekabbel (Bava Metzia 109b): "Scribe of the town" means one who counts [the number of] the townspeople, since here in the baraita it is called "scribe." Rather, it appears as Rabbeinu Chananel explained: "A scribe of the town" is one who writes the town's documents, and therefore below [Rava] considers it a loss that cannot be recovered, if a document is written improperly.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:9:1.hebrew: מתקנת יהושע בן גמלא ואילך לא ממטינן ינוקא ממתא למתא - וכגון שיש כאן כ"ה ינוקי שראויין להשכיר להם מלמד. ואם תאמר: הא אי הוה ממטינן להו למתא אחריתי יצטרכו מלמד בפני עצמן, כיון דאיכא כ"ה ינוקי; וא"כ, מאי נפקא מינה? וי"ל: דנפקא מינה, דאי הוו ב' מלמדי תינוקות באידך מתא, היו יכולין להושיב חציים בפני זה וחציים בפני זה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 21a:9:1.english: "From the ordinance of Yehoshua ben Gamla onward, we do not bring a child from town to town" - And [this applies] for example where there are twenty-five children here for whom it is fitting to hire a teacher. And if you say: But if we were to bring them to another town, they would need a teacher of their own, since there are twenty-five children; and if so, what difference does it make? And one can answer: There is a difference, for if there were two teachers of children in the other town, they could seat half [of the children] before this one and half before that one.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 21b:1:1.hebrew: פר"ח - דרביה אקרייה "זכר" כדין, והיינו "רמייה" דלא אשגח למידע היכי הוה קרי תלמידיה. וכן נראה. אבל אין נראה לפרש שגם רבו טעה ולימדו "זכר", דאם כן לאו "רמייה" הוא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 21b:1:1.english: Pirush Rabbeinu Chaim - His teacher taught him "zekher" properly, and this is the "negligence" [of the teacher]: that he did not take care to find out how his student was reading. And so it appears [correct]. But it does not seem right to explain that his teacher too erred and taught him "zakhar," for if so, it would not be negligence.
